concerns.message: Rule 1 of the workflow title rule (the latest run's `activity.feature`) renames the existing fixture workflows in the candidate phase. That contradicts the constraint that `currentCrumb` assertions stay unchanged. The PRD's claim that the fixture names are not generic only covers rules 2 and 3. In the candidate phase the server serves `activity.feature = run.inputs?.feature` (server/projects.ts:1028). Every seeded `feature-flow` run has inputs (seed.ts:282-347), with `feature: FEATURE_NAME = 'Review visibility and run inputs in the viewer'` (fixtures.ts:1275), while WORKFLOW_NAME is 'Feature flow'. Today `workflowTitle` (status.ts:67) applies only rules 2 and 3, which is why the suite is green.
concerns.consequence: Once the lists lane adds rule 1 to crumbs and headings, these fail in the candidate phase: projects.spec.ts:138 and :181 (`currentCrumb toHaveText(WORKFLOW_NAME)`), :135 and :136 (the workflows-list texts and the click by `^Feature flow`), and :149 (`Current definition graph of Feature flow`). So does lanes.spec.ts:182 (`workflows-list` toContainText [WORKFLOW_NAME, LANES_WORKFLOW_NAME]), and neither lane owns lanes.spec.ts, so it cannot be migrated. The worker-phase mocks serve no `activity`, so the lane passes its own worker run and then fails the verifier's candidate run. That leaves a choice between breaking the rule, a blocked lane, or editing a file outside its ownership.

concerns.message: The lists lane owns LiveStatus.tsx, NowBanner.tsx and CommandBlock.tsx, but none of them receives `activity` or `run_dir`. LiveStatus gets `{status, meta, now}` from RunHeader.tsx:89/138. NowBanner gets `{now, clock, focusHref}` from RunView.tsx:212. CommandBlock gets `{next}` from NowBanner, NodeHeader.tsx:194 and WorkerInputs.tsx:318. RunView.tsx and RunHeader.tsx belong to neither lane. The only owned path to the data is ProjectsView.tsx, which renders RunView with `detail`.
concerns.consequence: A worker that threads props will edit RunHeader.tsx or RunView.tsx and fail the ownership check. A worker that improvises may use a module-level side channel in api.ts. The `served-activity` scenario (the controller chip and the `RUN=` line) cannot be met through the existing props. The clean route is a React context provided in ProjectsView, following the `TimeReferenceContext` precedent in useNow.ts:117, and the task should say so. That route also puts the `RUN=` line into `node-next` and the answer blocks, which is intended but changes what the panels lane's `node-next` shows in worker-phase mocks for exposed runs.

concerns.message: Moving ReviewPanel onto `useRunReview` (as decisions.md requires) drops two behaviours of ReviewDetail.tsx:347-353. The first is the fallback path `paths.review(scope, attempt)` for exports whose review node has no `result_uri`. The second is the resource key that includes `node.status`, which re-asks when the node's status changes. The cache also stores `orNotRecorded`'s null as `ready`, and a `ready` entry is never re-fetched (useRunData.ts:51).
concerns.consequence: If NodeDetail passes only `result_uri`, as RunView.tsx:80 does, older exports without a link lose their review and show 'review-none'. If it passes the fallback path, a review node opened before its verdict caches null and keeps showing 'No review recorded' after the review lands, until a manual Refresh. That is a live-watch regression that no current test covers.

concerns.message: Only the `finding` test id is protected for the blocking card. Several other page-wide or exact-text assertions depend on what the card and the reviewer durations reuse: `page.getByTestId('finding-task-link')` toHaveCount(3) (inputs.spec.ts:193, lanes.spec.ts:140 and :239), page-level `review-verdict` and `review-blocked-by` toHaveText (review.spec.ts:109-115, reviewers.spec.ts:139-141), and exact `reviewer-status` text (reviewers.spec.ts:68, 148, 154).
concerns.consequence: If the card reuses FindingRow's requirement or file links, or adds a second `review-verdict`, the blocked-run assertions hit strict-mode or count failures. The three `finding-task-link` counts are on approved runs, so they survive only because those runs have no blocking card. Adding 'took 3m49s' or 'no verdict' inside `reviewer-status` breaks the exact-text checks, so durations must stay in their own element (as ReviewDetail.tsx:167 already does).

concerns.message: The reviewer strip already shows 'took <span>' from `launched_at` to `accepted_at` (ReviewDetail.tsx:155-167). The pending wording already contains 'no verdict recorded yet' (reviewers.ts:24).
concerns.consequence: Parts of `review-blocking-first` pass against the pre-change code, so the red run will not fail for those parts. The handoff's red evidence should name the assertions that actually fail (blocking card position, 'launch time not recorded', the 390 px cards), or it will look as if the test cannot detect the change.

structured_output.simpler_alternative: Reorder the title rule instead of adding rule 1 on top: generic `definition.name` ("Feature implementation") → the latest run's `activity.feature`, else the `workflow_id`; any other name → `definition.name`. `activity.feature` stays secondary text on Runs home rows and project cards. This fixes the live "Feature implementation" problem the PRD targets, keeps every `currentCrumb`, `workflows-list` and 'Current definition graph of …' assertion green in both phases, and needs no change to lanes.spec.ts, which no lane owns. Record it in decisions.md as an operator choice. Also tell the lists lane to deliver `activity` and `run_dir` through a React context provided in ProjectsView, following `TimeReferenceContext`, instead of threading props through RunView and RunHeader.
structured_output.cheap_experiment: Start the candidate-phase server with the existing seeds (no code change) and GET `/api/projects/<PROJECT>/workflows/feature-flow/runs`. Read `runs[0].activity.feature`: if it is 'Review visibility and run inputs in the viewer' rather than 'Feature flow', rule 1 as written breaks projects.spec.ts:138/181 and lanes.spec.ts:182. For end-to-end confirmation, temporarily make `workflowTitle` prefer that value and run `WORKFLOW_VERIFICATION_PHASE=candidate npx --no-install playwright test --config=tests/project-workflows/playwright.config.ts projects.spec.ts lanes.spec.ts`. It takes about a minute and decides whether the title rule has to be reordered before the lists worker starts.
